title: Beyond Earth
seo_title: Beyond Earth Class 6 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 12)
standard_text: Stars, constellations and the Pole Star; the apparent motion of stars; the Sun as a star; the solar system: planets, moons, asteroids and comets; artificial satellites and Indian space missions (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 12).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 6 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 12: stars and constellations, the Pole Star, the order of the planets, moons, asteroids and comets, and India's space missions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The Sun is a star; planets go round it.
key_sub: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
body_html:
How to think about it

Stars are huge balls of hot gas that give their own light; the Sun is the nearest star. Groups of stars that make patterns are constellations, such as Ursa Major (Saptarishi), Orion and Cassiopeia. Stars seem to move from east to west because the Earth rotates, but the Pole Star seems fixed in the north.

Eight planets go round the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Planets and moons shine by reflected sunlight. Asteroids lie between Mars and Jupiter, and comets grow tails near the Sun. India's Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole in 2023.

Example

Which planet is fifth from the Sun?

Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter

Answer: Jupiter

Example

Why do stars seem to move west?

the Earth spins

Answer: the Earth rotates from west to east

Common mistakes

  • Calling the Moon a star.
  • Thinking stars disappear in the day.
  • Calling Pluto the ninth planet.

faq.q: How can you tell a planet from a star?
faq.a: Stars twinkle, while planets usually shine steadily; planets also move slowly against the stars over many nights.

faq.q: Why does the Pole Star seem not to move?
faq.a: It lies almost directly above the Earth's North Pole, along the axis about which the Earth turns.
